description: Compute a Jacobi symbol for a canonical numerator and any bounded positive odd denominator using quadratic reciprocity without factoring.

source.title: Quadratic Reciprocity — The Jacobi Symbol; A Computational Introduction to Number Theory and Algebra, §12.3
source.author: Ben Lynn; Victor Shoup
source.reference: Stanford Pairing-Based Cryptography Notes, Quadratic Reciprocity; Shoup, version 2.0, §12.3.
source.implementation_status: Clean-room iterative reciprocity implementation; source descriptions only.

input.denominator_requirement: positive odd integer; composite values are accepted

output.encoding: Jacobi symbol -1 maps to 0, symbol 0 maps to 1, and symbol +1 maps to 2

contract.algorithm: Repeatedly remove powers of 2, applying (2/n)=(-1)^((n^2-1)/8), then swap numerator and denominator, apply quadratic reciprocity when both odd operands are 3 modulo 4, and reduce the new numerator modulo the new denominator.
contract.termination: Each swap replaces the denominator with a positive odd numerator smaller than the previous denominator; the loop ends at numerator zero.
contract.composite_semantics: The Jacobi symbol is defined through the prime factorization of the odd denominator, but the primary reciprocity algorithm does not factor it. A result of +1 for a composite denominator does not imply that the numerator is a square modulo that denominator.
contract.invalid_cases: Null, non-exact frame, negative or noncanonical numerator, zero or even denominator, and denominator above 1000000000 return -1.

complexity.time: O(log^2 n) bit operations for the Euclidean-like reciprocity loop
